subject: general
question: Tax, known as bhaga, was levied on which of the following during Mahajanapada period of Ancient India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tax on cultivators**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tax on cultivators (Bhaga):**
 
• Bhaga was a primary tax levied on agricultural produce during the Mahajanapada period.
 
• It was typically a share of the agricultural produce, often one-sixth (1/6th) of the yield.
 
• This tax was a major source of revenue for the rulers of the Mahajanapadas.
 
• The collection of bhaga was essential for maintaining the state's administration and military.
 
• This tax was a fundamental part of the agrarian economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tax on merchants:**
 
• While merchants were also taxed, the specific term "bhaga" was primarily associated with agricultural tax.
 
• Merchant taxes were generally in the form of customs duties or tolls.
 
• They paid taxes on goods that they sold.
 
• Trade was also a source of revenue.
 
• These taxes varied depending on the goods being traded.
 
• **Tax on artisans:**
 
• Artisans were also subject to taxation, but again, "bhaga" was not the term used.
 
• Artisans might have paid taxes in the form of labor or goods produced.
 
• Taxes on artisans were based on their crafts.
 
• They were an important part of the economy.
 
• They provided goods and services.
 
• **Tax on cattle breeders:**
 
• Cattle breeders were also taxed, but the term "bhaga" was not specifically used for them.
 
• Taxes on cattle breeders might have been levied on their livestock or dairy products.
 
• They paid taxes based on their livestock.
 
• Livestock was important to the economy.
 
• Cattle was considered wealth.
